notes: Loam — a design system for a fictional field-records platform used by habitat restoration crews. Single-page documentation + showcase built with semantic HTML and a CSS custom-property token system (6 colour ramps with semantic aliases, type scale with system font stacks, 4px spacing grid, radii, 3-step elevation ladder + focus ring, motion tokens, 4 breakpoints). 11 documented component families (buttons, links, badges/tags, alerts, form controls incl. radio cards and switches, cards, data display, tables, navigation, dialog/toast overlays, feedback states) each with usage guidance, do/don't examples and state coverage (hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, validation error/success). Two composed patterns: a validated 'create survey record' form (inline errors, aria-invalid/aria-describedby, focus to first invalid field, success alert) and a full site dashboard (stat cards, sortable/filterable/paginated table with row selection and bulk flagging, record detail dialog that mutates row status, species tab, key-value side cards, activity feed, progress, stepper). Minimal vanilla JS only (no frameworks, libraries or build step) powers tabs with arrow keys, native <dialog> (Esc, backdrop click, focus return), toasts via role=status, scrollspy, sidebar filter, mobile off-canvas nav, CSS-only tooltips and a live viewport indicator. Accessibility: skip link, single focus-ring token, keyboard-complete controls, contrast checked for AA on body/meta text. Known limitations: light theme only (dark theme deferred; tokens are layered to allow re-mapping), CSS-only tooltips do not reposition at viewport edges, no print styles, and 'View site' / notification-bell actions confirm via toast rather than navigating to pages outside the design-system scope.
